headline: High: firecrawl’s broad network egress and API-key handling can leak data or drive unsafe downstream actions when paired with local-only godot_rl_agents, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the pair’s lack of a documented shared…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl can ingest web content and expose it through API/MCP-style surfaces, while godot_rl_agents has no documented input bridge or shared channel. The pair lacks a proven default ingestion path, so prompt injection is possible mainly through unusual manual bridging or external orchestration, not by default.
conditions: IF an operator pipes firecrawl output into godot_rl_agents prompts or memory without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable any automatic prompt ingestion from firecrawl outputs.
Add a strict allowlist/stripper for instructions in scraped text.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces with no shared clipboard.
Review any MCP or queue bridge before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl touches API keys and broad web content and has broad network egress, while godot_rl_agents is local-only with no data classes listed. The pair does not show a shared workspace, but if firecrawl is pointed at sensitive inputs, its outbound API calls can transmit them off-box, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF firecrawl is given API keys, screenshots, or other sensitive files, those contents can be sent to its backend or external targets.
IF both agents are placed in the same workspace and files are copied between them, sensitive material can cross into outputs.
mitigations: Do not feed secrets or screenshots into firecrawl.
Rotate any API keys used in test runs.
Run firecrawl in a separate workspace from godot_rl_agents.
Block outbound traffic except to approved endpoints.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl supports multiple instances and has broad network egress, but godot_rl_agents shows no write, network, or mutable-resource surface. With no overlapping write targets or shared mutable state documented, direct capability conflict is limited and mostly requires external orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same mutable filesystem, git repo, or database, write conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator assigns both agents the same OAuth scope or API token, they may contend for shared resources.
mitigations: Assign separate directories and credentials.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo or database.
Serialize any shared-resource operations.
Check for hidden shared OAuth scopes before launch.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl can produce scraped web content and structured data, while godot_rl_agents is a runnable simulation stack that could consume upstream outputs if wired together. Because no verification or critique step is documented between them, bad or manipulated firecrawl output could cascade into downstream actions or training decisions.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents consumes firecrawl output as authoritative input, errors or injected facts can propagate.
IF an operator uses firecrawl-derived data to drive simulation parameters or decisions without validation, cascading failure is possible.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require schema checks on all firecrawl outputs.
Compare scraped facts against a second source before use.
Log and review rejected records.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl handles API keys and broad web content and is an open-source networked service, while godot_rl_agents is local-only and touches no listed sensitive data. The main compliance issue is residency/retention mismatch if firecrawl processes regulated content; the pair itself does not document a direct protected-data flow, so this is a moderate, not high, risk.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII or PHI is sent through firecrawl, residency and retention obligations may apply.
IF firecrawl logs or retains scraped content longer than policy allows, compliance gaps can arise.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through firecrawl.
Confirm retention settings before use.
Review logging for sensitive fields.
Keep godot_rl_agents isolated from regulated datasets.
requires-engineering: add policy-based redaction and retention controls.
